newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday May 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday May 6.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Italy's centre-left government said it had decided to call a confidence vote in the lower house of parliament to ram a controversial mini-budget past hundreds of opposition amendments (all).

* The decision to call a confidence vote was bitterly condemned by opposition parties. Hard right National Alliance party leader Gianfranco Fini called it intolerable and said it prevented parliamentary debate (all).

* Shares in clothing firm Marzotto closed fairly steady in Milan, while stocks in HPI dropped nearly seven percent on news that a planned merger between the two had been shelved. Marzotto closed up 0.07 percent, while shares in HPI, which was formed earlier this year, fell 6.97 percent. Industry minister Pierluigi Bersani called the failure of the merger a serious blow to Italy's financial and industrial system (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said Italy's public sector borrowing requirement in the first half of 1997 was expected to fall by more than 50 percent compared with the same period of 1996 (all).
* State-controlled energy giant Eni and electricity utility Enel said they had signed a letter of intent opening the way for the creation of a joint venture to produce electricity (all).

* Italcementi group, the largest cement producer in the European Union, said it posted 1996 consolidated profit of 87 billion lire against a previous 111 billion on sales of 5.142 trillion lire against 5.469 trillion (Sole 24 Ore).
* Swedish bicycle company Monark Stiga AB said on Monday it had signed an agreement with Italy's Piaggio group regarding the acquisition of bicycle company F.I.V. Edoardo Bianchi (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
